messages:
jonah: Seeing a weird trickle in ap-southeast1 -> lots of tiny-gpu pods stuck Pending, not classic quota. Warm-pool nodes show heartbeat lag around 15-20s. Anyone else?

devon: Yep saw it too. Preemptions up ~3x in the last 30m, some pods move AZ-to-AZ then go Pending again.

maya: throwing the grafana snapshot here: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/warmpool-heartbeats?orgId=1 (last 60m) — you can see heartbeat jitter at ~00:12 and a drift at 00:37.

jonah: thanks maya. Node-level logs show kubelet reconnects: `E kubelet: websocket read timeout` on a subset of warmpool hosts. Network retries are spiking.

sam: probable inter-AZ network blips? ap-southeast1b had a brief packet loss alert earlier from netops (~00:35). Could be correlated.

tara: netops confirmed a control-plane egress route flap tied to a load-balancer failover around that time. LB failed over to standby while healthchecks recovered.

devon: that matches. Scheduler kept binding pods to nodes that then failed the kubelet health check, so they got preempted and requeued. Result: fragmentation of small-slot GPU capacity.

jonah: quick mitigation idea: throttle scheduler's bind rate for tiny-gpu class to avoid churn + mark affected warmpool nodes temporarily unschedulable so pods don't bounce. Thoughts? :thinking: 

maya: agree. We can push a small canary: change `--bind-rate=20` -> `--bind-rate=5` for scheduler in ap-southeast1 (canary on 2 replicas). Also add a taint `taint.k8s.io/warmpool-limbo=true:NoSchedule` on nodes showing kubelet flakiness, then drain gracefully.

sam: +1. Also we should consider enabling `PreferNoSchedule` pod affinity for tiny-gpu to avoid cross-AZ hops during transient net issues.

devon: quick command snippets if folks want to run now: 
```
# mark node unschedulable warmpool hosts with flaky kubelet
kubectl taint nodes node-abc warmpool-limbo=true:NoSchedule --overwrite
kubectl cordon node-abc && kubectl drain node-abc --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```

jonah: infra-bot shows current warmpool pool size: 12 nodes, warm replicas 8. If we cordon 2-3 nodes we'll need to temporarily scale warmpool to 14 to keep capacity.

infra-bot: [autoscaler] warmpool-ap-southeast1 target increased from 12 -> 14 (requested by @jonah) — rollout in progress.

tara: netops will keep an eye on LB healthchecks. We'll also open a support ticket with cloud provider for ephemeral route flaps.

maya: after we stabilize, follow-up work: scheduler should detect repeated bind/fail cycles and backoff per pod group (avoid immediate rebind across AZ). Filing a ticket.

devon: filing: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4021 — "scheduler: bind backoff for repeated node failure during bind -> reduces tiny-gpu fragmentation". Assigning to eng-platform.

jonah: ok doing the canary bind-rate change now on the ap-southeast1 scheduler rollout. I'll monitor pending queue and preemption rate for 15m.

sam: if preemptions drop and pending clears, we can roll to rest of region. If not, we'll revert and try the taint/drain path. :thumbsup: 

jonah: update (00:50): preemptions down 60%, pending count decreasing. Looks promising. Will keep monitoring.

maya: nice. Follow-up action list: 1) scheduler backoff RFC 2) affinity tweak for tiny-gpu pods 3) warmpool heartbeat alert tune to fire earlier 4) postmortem if cloud provider confirms LB flap.

tara: netops: we've escalated to provider, ticket ID: CLOUD-99823. Adding logs and traceroutes.

devon: thanks everyone. I'll capture fixes in INF-4021 and add the canary rollout notes.

jonah: closing loop here once provider confirms. For now region looks stable and fragmentation is healing. :relieved:
